EnglishExample: I studied for two hours.
Explanation: Use por when describing how long something lasted.

SpanishExample: El vuelo se canceló por la tormenta.
EnglishExample: The flight was canceled because of the storm.
Explanation: Use por to explain why something happened.

SpanishExample: Pagué veinte dólares por la camiseta.
EnglishExample: I paid twenty dollars for the shirt.
Explanation: Use por when one thing is traded or paid for another.

Rule: Movement through or along a place
EnglishExample: We walked through the park.
Explanation: Use por for motion passing through, along, or around a place.

SpanishExample: Te envié la información por correo electrónico.
EnglishExample: I sent you the information by email.
Explanation: Use por for the medium or mode used.

SpanishExample: Voy al gimnasio tres veces por semana.
EnglishExample: I go to the gym three times per week.
Explanation: Use por to express a rate.

Rule: On behalf of or in place of someone
EnglishExample: Can you work in my place on Friday?
Explanation: Use por when substituting for or acting on behalf of someone.

SpanishExample: La novela fue escrita por García Márquez.
EnglishExample: The novel was written by García Márquez.
Explanation: Use por to introduce who performed the action in a passive sentence.

Rule: In search of / to fetch (with ir, venir, pasar)
EnglishExample: I'm going to get water.
Explanation: Use por after motion verbs when the meaning is 'to go fetch.'

EnglishExample: Thanks for your help.
Explanation: Use por after gracias to state what you are thankful for.

EnglishExample: We'll arrive around eight.
Explanation: Use por for vague or approximate times and places.

EnglishExample: Five times five is twenty-five.
Explanation: Use por for the multiplication operator.

Rule: Emotion or motive toward something ("for" as motivation)
EnglishExample: I do it for love / out of love.
Explanation: Use por when the feeling or motive drives the action.

EnglishExample: I leave for Madrid tomorrow.
Explanation: Use para when indicating where someone or something is headed.

Rule: Deadline or specific point in time ("by / due")
SpanishExample: El informe es para el lunes.
EnglishExample: The report is due by Monday.
Explanation: Use para when something must be completed by a certain time.

Rule: Purpose or goal ("in order to" + infinitive)
EnglishExample: I study in order to pass the exam.
Explanation: Use para before an infinitive to express the goal of an action.

EnglishExample: This gift is for you.
Explanation: Use para to indicate who will receive something.

SpanishExample: Para mí, la honestidad es lo más importante.
EnglishExample: In my opinion, honesty is the most important thing.
Explanation: Use para + pronoun to frame a personal perspective.

SpanishExample: Para ser principiante, cocinas muy bien.
EnglishExample: For a beginner, you cook very well.
Explanation: Use para to set up an unexpected contrast.

SpanishExample: Trabajo para una empresa de tecnología.
EnglishExample: I work for a tech company.
Explanation: Use para when stating who you are employed by.

EnglishExample: This cup is for coffee.
Explanation: Use para to describe what something is designed or intended for.

Rule: Readiness or being about to (estar para)
EnglishExample: The train is about to leave.
Explanation: Use estar + para + infinitive to express that something is on the verge of happening.
